checks.result: The causal clause expressly concerns corresponding Destatis data and calculators being tied to calendar years, after describing additional difficulty at under-year tenancy starts. It is a factual supporting reason rather than merely the broad judgment that a stepped statutory formula is complex.

The dated manual expressly includes calendar-month as well as annual calculations with flexible beginning/end points; p48 demonstrates a May2020–October2022comparison. Thus an available monthly/non-calendar-year aid precedes the2026hearing.

The existing programme is not shown to calculate the proposed half-excess annual thresholds and pro-rata cap. The bill p18 itself anticipates adaptation, and p25 applies full-year periods beginning at tenancy/last increase plus complete-month remainders. This rescues a claim of additional legal calculation or usability difficulty, but not the stated existing calendar-year data restriction.

Summaryphysicalp4 explicitly requests a lower absolute limit; physicalp10 repeats criticism of the half-excess mechanism. The erroneous supporting reason favours that simplification request, but correction does not settle accessibility, complexity or the appropriate cap. Minor is proportionate.
